answer: Each agent can earn voting weight only through a time-locked stake that is slashed if it certifies a dishonest task result. A newcomer’s claim is checked by randomly assigned, independently bonded agents, with rewards delayed until the work is audited. Creating a hundred identities therefore does not create a hundred cheap votes: the attacker must lock substantial capital in each and risks losing it when caught. A raven alert can travel along a vine of attestations to a trusted bridge between reviewer groups, prompting a fresh audit before rewards clear.
